title: Improve quant kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion + KV cache & batching scheduling
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Quantized inference is a major lever for reducing token cost but we observed two practical gaps in production: (1) suboptimal kernel shapes and extra dequant/quantize memory hops for mixed FP8/INT8 serving paths, and (2) lower utilization for short sequences due to the current batching and KV-cache layout for quantized tensors. This PR implements a set of runtime and kernel changes to address both areas: - fused dequant + GEMM kernels for INT8/FP8 paths (CUDA/CPU fallbacks) to remove intermediate buffer copies and improve arithmetic intensity; - integrate SmoothQuant scaling into the quantization pipeline so per-channel scaling is applied pre-quantize instead of as a separate pointwise op; - dequant-fusion fallbacks that preserve quantized KV cache layout to avoid repeated quantize/dequant on cache hits; - scheduler updates for continuous batching that coalesces short, quantized requests into larger GEMM-friendly batches while respecting latency SLOs; - KV cache layout change (quantized-packed layout) and small indexing shim so existing downstream code continues to address caches transparently. Changes are implemented with careful feature flags and a runtime compatibility check: the fused kernels are selected when the model variant is marked quantized and SmoothQuant metadata is present. Benchmarks included compare the old path (separate quantize/dequant + generic GEMM) vs new fused path across INT8 and FP8 variants on A100-80GB and 4xA100 multi-GPU setups. Safety: Adds unit tests for kernel numerics (relative error thresholds), integration tests for KV cache correctness, and gated rollout flags. Rollout plan: rolling canary to 10% of traffic on dedicated before global launch.

benchmark_summary: Testbed: single A100-80GB and 4xA100 cluster, models: redwood/v1-medium quantized INT8 and FP8 variants, sequence lengths 32/64/256, batch sizes tuned by continuous batching. Results: - End-to-end tokens/sec improved by 18-28% on INT8 paths and 12-20% on FP8 paths for common seqlen 64 workload. - Median tail latency (p95) reduced by ~12% on INT8; p99 improved 9%. - Fused dequant+GEMM kernel shows 1.6x effective kernel throughput vs prior two-stage path for large matmuls and 1.2-1.3x for small shapes due to reduced memory copies. - KV cache hits avoid ~2.5x worth of quantize/dequant memory traffic leading to CPU/GPU memory bandwidth savings and improved throughput under multi-tenant load. Measurement methodology: 50 runs for each config, warmup 2000 tokens, measurement windows with and without cache warm state. Detailed CSVs attached to perf artifact.
merge_details: Squash merge by Lin Zhao. Merge commit: squash into main with message 'Optimize quant kernels: fused dequant+GEMM, SmoothQuant integration, KV cache & continuous batching improvements (ENG-1284, ENG-1307)'. Canary rollout to 10% dedicated traffic followed by full rollout after 48h.
release_notes: Performance: Improved quantized inference throughput and latency for INT8/FP8 models via fused dequant+GEMM kernels and SmoothQuant integration; KV cache improvements reduce memory traffic for quantized models. Rollout: gated canary in dedicated clusters, enable via runtime flag 'quant_fused_kernels=enabled'.
notes: Feature gated and behind runtime compatibility checks. We added a telemetry signal 'quant_fused_kernel_enabled' and per-model 'smoothquant_metadata' to avoid accidental mis-selection. Follow-up work: expand CPU vectorized kernels, add AMX tiled kernels for on-prem hardware, and add auto-tuning step in the compile step for fused kernels.
